Tier 1.threshold: Trend stable or increasing (1960-2021) and average total storage > reference scenario.

policies.note: No state intervention under normal conditions.
Permits issued for diversions during storm events to enhance groundwater recharge.
Funding encouraged as contingency for emergency water supply.

Tier 2.threshold: Trend stable or increasing, but average total storage < reference scenario.

policies.note: Triggered if critical or long-term overdraft occurs, GSP fails or is not implemented, or significant surface water depletion occurs.
Permits continue to be issued as in Tier 1.

Tier 3.threshold: Trend declining at moderate rate; fitted slope > -0.015 ft/yr.

policies.note: Intervention remains unlikely unless overdraft or GSP issues persist.

policies.policy_name: GSA curtailments, pumping limits, and fees
policies.note: Local GSAs implement curtailments, pumping restrictions, and fees to prevent overpumping.
Permits continue as in previous tiers.
Funding continues as in previous tiers.

Tier 4.threshold: Trend declining more severely; slope <= -0.015 ft/yr.

policies.note: Critical overdraft, failed GSP implementation, or significant surface water depletion necessitate state intervention.
Permits continue as in previous tiers.
Funding continues as in previous tiers.
